title_options: Could A T. rex See You Standing Still? 🦖
facts: Stevens 2006, Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology 26(2):321-330, 'Binocular vision in theropod dinosaurs': from sculpted head reconstructions, Tyrannosaurus had a binocular field of about 55 degrees, wider than modern hawks (press reports of the study); acuity and far point estimated from reptile and bird models: objects possibly visible at about 6 km versus about 1.6 km for people (model estimate).
description: The famous movie line says stand still and a T. rex can't see you. A study of its skull says it probably could. #shorts #dinosaurs #TRex #Science
sources: Stevens 2006, 'Binocular vision in theropod dinosaurs', Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology 26(2):321-330.

scenes.narration: Standing still probably wouldn't hide you from a T. rex.
Scientists rebuilt its head and traced where each eye could look.
Its eyes faced forward, overlapping across about fifty-five degrees, wider than a hawk's.
That overlap gives depth vision, perfect for judging exactly how far away you are.
It may have spotted things about six kilometres away. People manage about one and a half.
So if standing still won't work, what would you do?
